blocks.text: The opening charge defines Timothy’s work in active terms: proclaim, persist, correct, rebuke, encourage, teach patiently, stay clear-minded, endure hardship, evangelize, and complete his service. The warning about people seeking teachers who suit their own desires explains why this ministry requires both patience and firmness.

The chapter combines warning with practical, personal requests. Its criticism of people who turn from truth toward myths stands alongside requests for Timothy, Mark, a cloak, books, and parchments. These details keep the letter’s final exhortations connected to concrete needs and relationships rather than presenting them as abstract instruction alone.

The speaker presents his departure as near, describes a completed fight and race, recalls an unsupported first defense, and names many coworkers in the closing. Modern scholarship offers differing explanations of the letter’s authorship and setting, including direct Pauline, secretary-assisted, composite, and Pauline-school accounts. Consequently, the chapter’s farewell and expected death are central features of its voice, while conclusions about their precise historical circumstances remain disputed.

The broader letter has been compared with a farewell or testament: it includes warning, a final charge, exemplary memory, succession, and an anticipated death. That comparison is plausible but disputed, as are questions about form and historicity. For the text’s transmission, Codex Sinaiticus preserves 2 Timothy, whereas the surviving Codex Vaticanus ends before the Pastoral Epistles and therefore is not a witness to this book.
